subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Actuators: The Muscles of Robots
description: A quick, practical guide to Actuators: The Muscles of Robots.

hook.text: Every robot joint needs a motor. Electric servos, hydraulic cylinders, and pneumatic actuators each bring different strengths.

buildup.text: Electric servo motors dominate robotics. They offer precise speed and position control with compact size.

discovery.text: Hydraulic actuators deliver enormous force in a small package. Heavy-lift robots and walking machines use them.

twist.text: Pneumatic actuators are fast but imprecise. They're great for binary tasks — open/close, extend/retract — but not for positioning.

climax.text: New artificial muscles made from electroactive polymers flex like real tissue. Soft robotics is emerging.

punchline.text: The actuator defines the robot's strength, speed, and precision. Choose wisely.

quiz.question: Why do most industrial robots use electric servo motors?
options: They produce more force than hydraulic systems at lower cost
They offer precise speed and position control in a compact package
They require no maintenance and last forever without replacement
